statement.p: One of the tires on your car looks a little flat. You measure its air pressure and are alarmed to see it so low at {21\ {\rm psi}}\text{.} You have a portable device that can pump air into the tire increasing the pressure at a rate of {1.7\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut psi}{\rm\mathstrut min}}}\text{.} How long will it take to fill the tire to the manuals recommended pressure of {32\ {\rm psi}}\text{?}

solution.p: This is a rate scenario. The air pressure starts out at 21\text{,} and increases with a rate of 1.7\text{.} Eventually the pressure reaches 32\text{.} So the equation we set up is: 21+1.7t=32 where t is the number of minutes the pump runs. Now we follow the standard steps to solve this equation. \begin{aligned} 21+1.7t \amp= 32\\ 21+1.7t-21 \amp= 32-21\\ 1.7t \amp= 11\\ \frac{1.7t}{1.7} \amp= \frac{11}{1.7}\\ t \amp = 6.47058823529412 \end{aligned} So it will take {6.47059\ {\rm min}} for the pump to fill the tire.
